searchText: Has anyone tried eth2-comply? I'm looking test prysm's new eth2api implementations conforms to the standard https://blog.infura.io/new-open-source-tool-testing-api-conformance-eth2-comply/ <@363800010518822915> I'm fairly certain that <@680234424037670912> is using eth2-comply (he'll be along in a bit to confirm or deny 🙂). If you have any feedback on it, I meet weekly with that team and would happily pass it along. Thanks! we'll try it out and let you know how it goes. Really grateful to have Infura providing such a wonderful tool <@!363800010518822915> I've been using eth2-comply, and it's been a good source of validation. It's young, but I think if we keep using it and improving what's there, it'll be a great way to validate the APIs are relatively consistent. Currently teku hasn't got all of the standard api's so I get a fair number of errors obviously, but at least I can check the outputs of the ones that I do have. I've even been cutting down the tests that get run so that I can just focus on what I have at the moment in the standard api set :) I've found a couple of issues as i've been using it, and they've been fixed in a pretty quick turn around, which is great! test cases are json, so mostly easy to update
